title: Residue identifications of powered parameter quotients
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\Lambda$ a commutative $k$-algebra, $d,c\in\mathbb N$, $c\ge1$, $P=k[X_i\mid i\in\operatorname{Fin}(d)]$, $\varphi:P\to\Lambda$ a $k$-algebra map, and $q\subset\Lambda$ a prime. Suppose the images of $\varphi(X_i)$ generate the maximal ideal of $\Lambda_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Put $J=((X_i^c)^8)$, $J_\Lambda=J\Lambda$. For every prime $q_0\subset\Lambda/J_\Lambda$ contracting to $q$, put $p_0=q_0\cap(P/J)$, $R_0=(P/J)_{p_0}$, $L_0=(\Lambda/J_\Lambda)_{q_0}$, $L=\operatorname{ULift}(L_0)$, and $I=\mathfrak m_{R_0}$. There exist ring isomorphisms $e_R:R_0/I\simeq k$ and $e_L:L/IL\simeq\kappa(q)$ such that $e_L(r\cdot1)=\operatorname{algebraMap}_{k,\kappa(q)}(e_R(r))$ for every $r\in R_0/I$. No regularity, dimension or separability hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Maximal-ideal contraction puts each φ(X_i) in q. Thus φ⁻¹(q) contains the variable ideal, which is maximal with quotient k by evaluation at zero, so it equals that ideal. Since c≥1, J is contained in it.

Prime contraction through the quotient square gives the inverse image of p₀ as the variable ideal. The quotient/localization isomorphism identifies R₀ with P_p/JP_p. Its maximal ideal is the image of pP_p. The third isomorphism theorem reduces R₀/I to P_p/pP_p=P/p=k; the last map sends constants to themselves.

Identify L₀ with Λ_q/JΛ_q by localization of the quotient. The maximal ideal is the image of the maximal ideal of Λ_q. The image of I is generated by the φ(X_i); the generation hypothesis makes it that maximal ideal. The third isomorphism theorem gives L₀/IL₀=κ(q). ULift.down induces the corresponding quotient ring isomorphism for L.

The quotient maps, fractions and residue maps preserve constants. On a polynomial class both scalar maps send every variable to zero and every constant to its given image in κ(q). This equality extends across localization because maps agree on inverses. These are the required compatible e_R and e_L. When d=0 all variable ideals are zero and the generation hypothesis makes Λ_q a field.

theorem parameter_quotient_residue_ringEquivs
    {k : Type u} {Λ : Type w} [Field k] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ]
    (d c : ℕ) (hc : 1 ≤ c) (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin d) k →ₐ[k] Λ)
    (q : PrimeSpectrum Λ)
    (hgen : Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin d ↦
      algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) (φ (MvPolynomial.X i)))) =
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)) :
    letI := φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    let J : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) :=
      Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin d ↦ (MvPolynomial.X i ^ c) ^ 8))
    let J_Λ := Ideal.map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) Λ) J
    ∀ (q₀ : PrimeSpectrum (Λ ⧸ J_Λ)),
      PrimeSpectrum.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk J_Λ) q₀ = q →
    letI := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver
      (q₀.asIdeal.under (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k ⧸ J)) q₀.asIdeal
    let R₀ := Localization.AtPrime (q₀.asIdeal.under (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k ⧸ J))
    let L₀ := Localization.AtPrime q₀.asIdeal
    let L := ULift.{max u v} L₀
    let I := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R₀
    ∃ eR : (R₀ ⧸ I) ≃+* k,
      ∃ eL : (L ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R₀ L)) ≃+* q.asIdeal.ResidueField,
        ∀ r : R₀ ⧸ I,
          eL (algebraMap (R₀ ⧸ I) (L ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R₀ L)) r) =
            algebraMap k q.asIdeal.ResidueField (eR r)
